title: CompTIA Network+ (N10-009)
summary: CompTIA Network+, exam code N10-009, is a vendor neutral certification for people who build and support the networks that everything else runs on. It sits at a foundation level, above basic IT support and before specialist security or cloud exams, and it suits help desk staff, junior administrators and career changers. Passing it tells an employer that you understand how data moves between systems, that you can configure and explain common network devices, and that you can diagnose a connectivity fault methodically. The exam is proctored and mixes multiple choice and multiple response questions with performance based items that present a scenario with several correct actions to choose. It leads to roles such as network technician, network administrator, support engineer and network operations centre analyst, and it is a common stepping stone to Security+. The domain list below follows the published objectives, so check the current version with CompTIA before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CompTIA.

beginner.definition: This is a foundation certificate from CompTIA about computer networking. A network is a group of computers and devices that share data, such as the internet in an office. Network+ proves you understand how that sharing works, how devices are configured and how to find faults.
beginner.whyItMatters: Almost every security problem involves a network, and almost every outage starts as a connectivity problem. Employers want people who can explain addresses, routes and ports without guessing. This certificate is often the first serious step from a support desk into an infrastructure or security team. It also builds the base for cloud and cyber security study later.
howItWorks: Learn how data is packaged and sent, starting with the layered model that describes each step.
Study addresses and names, including internet protocol addresses, subnet masks and domain name resolution.
Build a small home lab with a switch, a router and two virtual machines so you can watch real traffic.
Learn the tools you will use daily, such as ping, traceroute, address lookup and a packet capture program.
Study wireless, virtual private networks, cloud connectivity and basic network security controls.
Practise scenario questions, then sit the proctored exam, which includes questions with more than one required action.
beginner.example: Think about posting a letter to a friend in another city. You write the address, and the post office sorts it. Lorries move it along roads until it reaches the right flat. Your friend must be at home to receive it, and a reply travels back the same way. A computer network works like that postal service. Internet protocol addresses replace street names, and routers replace sorting offices. Network+ teaches you the whole postal system, not just one letter.
takeaways: Learn the layered model well, because almost every other topic hangs from it.
Hands on practice with real devices or a simulator makes the addressing topics much easier.
Check the current exam objectives on the CompTIA website, because a newer version may be live.

objectives: Explain how data moves across a network using layered models and common protocols
Configure addressing, routing, switching and wireless settings for a small network
Describe cloud and virtual networking concepts and how they connect to a physical network
Apply network security controls that reduce the chance of a successful attack
Monitor, document and change a network using recognised operational practices
Troubleshoot connectivity and performance faults with a structured method and the right tools

chapters.title: Networking concepts
objectives: Explain the layers of the networking model and what each layer is responsible for
Describe how common protocols and ports are used to carry traffic such as web, mail and file transfer
Compare network types and topologies, including local, wide area and software defined networks
Explain how internet protocol addressing and subnetting group devices into networks
Describe name resolution and the services that turn a name into an address
Explain how the physical medium, including copper, fibre and wireless, affects speed and distance
Describe how cloud services and virtual networks change the traditional network diagram

chapters.title: Network implementation
objectives: Configure switches, including virtual local area networks, trunk links and spanning tree protection
Configure routers and compare dynamic routing approaches with static routes
Set up wireless networks with appropriate channels, bands and authentication settings
Explain how a device obtains an address automatically and how that service is made resilient
Describe wide area, virtual private network and remote access options for connecting sites
Explain how network devices are placed and cabled so that traffic is reliable and easy to support

chapters.title: Network operations
objectives: Apply a documented change process so that network changes can be reversed
Monitor network health with performance measures, alerts and log data
Keep accurate diagrams, address plans and asset records, and explain why each matters
Describe the policies that govern network use, access and acceptable behaviour
Explain how high availability and redundancy are provided for critical network paths
Describe remote management access and the safeguards that protect it

chapters.title: Network security
objectives: Explain common network attacks, including spoofing, on-path interception and denial of service
Place firewalls, intrusion detection and access control so that they protect the right boundary
Describe authentication, authorisation and accounting for network access
Explain how encryption protects data in transit and how certificates support it
Apply hardening practices to network devices, including secure management and patching
Describe how physical security and environmental controls protect network equipment

chapters.title: Network troubleshooting
objectives: Follow a documented troubleshooting method and identify the problem before changing anything
Use command line tools to test addressing, routing, name resolution and reachability
Capture and read network traffic to prove where a conversation fails
Diagnose common faults such as a duplicate address, a wrong virtual local area network or a bad cable
Diagnose wireless problems such as weak signal, interference and authentication failure
Confirm that a fix works, record the cause and update the documentation
